title: Maui Fishes Up the Land
text:
The Maori tell that the demigod Maui wanted to go fishing with his older brothers, but they refused to take him. So he hid in the bottom of their canoe, and when they were far out at sea, he revealed himself. They were angry, but by then it was too late to turn back.

Maui made them paddle farther than they had ever gone. Then he took out a magic fishhook made from the jawbone of his ancestor. His brothers would not give him bait, so he struck his own nose and smeared the hook with his blood. He let it down into the deep, and soon it caught on something vast. Chanting, Maui hauled it up: an enormous fish, so large it was a whole land.

Before he left, Maui told his brothers not to touch the fish until he had gone to make an offering to the gods and returned. But as soon as he was gone, the brothers began cutting it up and eating it. The fish writhed and thrashed under their knives. That, the story says, is why the North Island of New Zealand, Te Ika a Maui, the Fish of Maui, is full of mountains and valleys instead of being flat.
lesson: A team that breaks the agreed plan as soon as the leader looks away can spoil what it has won together. Discipline matters most just after success.
source: George Grey, Polynesian Mythology (1855), The Legend of Maui
